title: Evaluation-transpose construction of equivariant Verdier exchange
statement:
Fix primes $p\ne\ell$, $a\ge1$, $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, an algebraic closure $k$ of $k_0$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in a fixed algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, and $\Lambda\in\{E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. For a finite-type $k_0$-scheme $T_0$ put $T=T_0\times_{k_0}k$, $g_T=\operatorname{id}_{T_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\operatorname{Frob}_q)$ with geometric Frobenius, and $P_T=Lg_T^*$ [def-weil-frobenius-detailed, def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Use the rational/common-stage bounded constructible categories and Weil pairs $(K,\theta_K:P_TK\xrightarrow{\sim}K)$, whose arrows satisfy $u\theta_K=\theta_LP_T(u)$ [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. Let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be a separated finite-type morphism of finite-type $k_0$-schemes, and put $f=f_0\times_{k_0}k:X\to Y$. Assume $X_0,Y_0$ separated for the duality assertions. For $T=X,Y$ put $a_T:T\to s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $\omega_T=Ra_T^!\Lambda_s$, and $D_T=R\mathcal Hom_T(-,\omega_T)$, using the constructible exceptional adjoint [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. Use the canonical Weil lifts of the operations and their adjunctions, with equivariant units, counits, tensor evaluation and compact-support composition comparisons. Then $D_T$ lifts contravariantly to rational Weil pairs, its evaluation and biduality are equivariant, and the canonical comparisons
$$ \omega_{T,E}\otimes_E L\simeq\omega_{T,L},\qquad (D_{T,E}K)\otimes_E L\simeq D_{T,L}(K\otimes_E L) $$
for every finite $E\subset L\subset\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ are equivariant, together with their evaluation, biduality and adjunction diagrams, also in the common-stage category.

Let $M$ be a Weil object on a domain where all following objects, tensor–Hom adjunctions, exceptional and ordinary adjunctions, and the displayed projection isomorphism are defined. Put $A=R\mathcal Hom_Y(Rf_!M,\omega_Y)$. Form
$$ Rf_!(M\otimes^LLf^*A)\xrightarrow{\operatorname{PF}^{-1}}Rf_!M\otimes^LA\xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}}\omega_Y, $$
where $\operatorname{PF}$ is the specified projection map [def-exchange-projection], using the canonical tensor symmetry for evaluation if needed. Its successive exceptional, tensor–Hom and ordinary adjunction transposes define
$$ A\longrightarrow Rf_*R\mathcal Hom_X(M,Rf^!\omega_Y). $$
Let $c:Rf^!\omega_Y\simeq\omega_X$ be the mate of compact-support composition $a_X=a_Yf$, evaluated at the coefficient unit [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. Postcompose with $Rf_*R\mathcal Hom(M,c)$. This specific formal map
$$ D_YRf_!M\longrightarrow Rf_*D_XM $$
is equivariant. Each transpose is application of the corresponding lifted right adjoint after its unit; the mate expression for $c$ uses those units and counits and the pasting-compatible composition comparison. Under the hypotheses of [fix-lem-tensor-adjunction, fix-cor-verdier-exchange] the map is the inverse internal-adjunction isomorphism followed by $Rf_*R\mathcal Hom(M,c)$, so those theorems make it invertible and its inverse is equivariant. More generally equivariance holds wherever this same formal map and the displayed data exist, without claiming invertibility there or adding ambient exceptional-adjoint admissibility to the operation-lifting assertion. These identities use rational Weil isomorphisms themselves and require no invariant integral lattice.

proof.text: Apply [cor-coef-verdier-weil-equivariance] to each of $T_0=X_0,Y_0$. Its hypotheses are exactly the separated finite-type finite-field and rational/common-stage coefficient hypotheses here. It gives the contravariant Weil lift of $D_T$, equivariance of evaluation and biduality, and the dualizing/duality scalar-extension comparisons together with their evaluation, biduality and exceptional-adjunction diagrams. In particular $A=D_YRf_!M$ has its specified Weil structure whenever $Rf_!M$ is in the stated constructible domain. For orientation only (nothing below uses the formula): writing $h_T:P_TR\mathcal Hom(K,\omega_T)\simeq R\mathcal Hom(P_TK,P_T\omega_T)$, the structure $R\mathcal Hom(\theta_K^{-1},\theta_{\omega_T})h_T$ makes evaluation equivariant, since $\operatorname{ev}(\theta_Kx,\theta_D\varphi)=\theta_{\omega_T}((h_T\varphi)(\theta_K^{-1}\theta_Kx))$; it uses the rational isomorphism $\theta_K$ itself. Steps 2--8 use only the equivariance assertions of the corollary. The cited corollary also gives these assertions in the common-stage category without a stable integral lattice.

source.place: Sentence 4: duality and evaluation; preliminary rational/common-stage assertions.

proof.text: Write $F=Rf_!$, $G=Rf^!$, $P=Lf^*$ and $Q=Rf_*$, and put $V=M\otimes^L PA$. The projection isomorphism $\operatorname{PF}:FM\otimes^L A\xrightarrow{\sim}FV$ of [def-exchange-projection] is a morphism of Weil pairs on this domain by [lem-pod-constructible-mate-coherence], whose statement makes the projection transformation of [def-exchange-projection] a Weil morphism on its constructible domains for the same separated finite-type $f_0$ and the same rational/common-stage Weil pairs; its invertibility is the hypothesis of the item, not a consequence of equivariance. Its inverse is a Weil morphism: if $u\theta_B=\theta_CP_Y(u)$, multiplication by $u^{-1}$ on the left and $P_Y(u^{-1})$ on the right gives $u^{-1}\theta_C=\theta_BP_Y(u^{-1})$. The evaluation $FM\otimes^L D_YFM\to\omega_Y$ is equivariant by Step 1. Consequently $b=\operatorname{ev}\circ\operatorname{PF}^{-1}:FV\to\omega_Y$ is equivariant. Indeed for two composable Weil arrows $u,v$, $(vu)\theta=v\theta'P_Y(u)=\theta''P_Y(vu)$, the defining equation of [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. The displayed evaluation uses the $FM\otimes A$ order, so no symmetry needs to be inserted.

For the assumed lifted exceptional adjunction $F\dashv G$, with unit $\eta^!$, the first transpose is exactly $t=G(b)\circ\eta^!_V:V\to G\omega_Y$. Both factors are arrows of Weil pairs: $G(b)$ because $G$ is the supplied lifted functor, and $\eta^!_V$ because its unit is assumed equivariant. Thus $t$ is equivariant by the composition equation of Step 2. This only uses the constructible lifted adjunction stipulated in the statement, and does not assume an ambient exceptional right adjoint.

Let $H_M=R\mathcal Hom_X(M,-)$ and let $
u$ be the unit of the stipulated lifted adjunction $M\otimes^L-\dashv H_M$. The second transpose is $r=H_M(t)\circ
u_{PA}:PA	o H_M(G\omega_Y)$. Its factors are Weil arrows by functoriality of the lifted $H_M$ and equivariance of $
u$. For the lifted ordinary adjunction $P\dashv Q$ with unit $\eta^*$ the third transpose is $s=Q(r)\circ\eta^*_A:A	o QH_M(G\omega_Y)$. The same two assertions for $Q$ and $\eta^*$ make $s$ equivariant. These are the unit-then-right-adjoint formulas for the given adjunction bijections, so their underlying maps are precisely the successive transposes specified in the statement.

source.place: Sentence 4: tensor–Hom and ordinary adjunction transposes.

proof.text:
Here is the mate expression for $c$. Set $H=Ra_Y{}_!$, $J=Ra_Y^!$, $U=Ra_X{}_!$, $W=Ra_X^!$, and let $\alpha:HF\xrightarrow{\sim}U$ be the stipulated compact-support compositor. The counit of the pasted adjunction $HF\dashv GJ$ is $\varepsilon^{HF}_Z=\varepsilon^H_Z\circ H(\varepsilon^F_{JZ})$. Transposing $\varepsilon^{HF}_Z\circ\alpha^{-1}_{GJZ}:U(GJZ)\to Z$ through $U\dashv W$ gives
$$c_Z=W(\varepsilon^{HF}_Z\circ\alpha^{-1}_{GJZ})\circ\eta^U_{GJZ}:GJZ\longrightarrow WZ.$$
This is the unit–map–counit mate formula of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], applied to $\alpha^{-1}:U\to HF$ and the pasted adjunction. Each unit, counit and $\alpha$ is equivariant by hypothesis, its inverse is equivariant by Step 2, and the displayed lifted functors preserve Weil arrows. Hence $c_Z$ is equivariant. At $Z=\Lambda_s$, with its coefficient-unit Weil structure, this is the specified $c:G\omega_Y\simeq\omega_X$. The specified compositor and pasted adjunctions fix this mate; no independent choice of dualizing identification is being made.

source.place: Sentence 4: structure-morphism comparison as the mate of compact-support composition.

proof.text:
The given lift of $H_M$ sends the Weil arrow $c$ to $H_M(c)$, and the given lift of $Q$ sends that arrow to $QH_M(c)$. Thus
$$e_M=QH_M(c)\circ s:D_YFM\longrightarrow QD_XM$$
is equivariant, by Steps 4–5 and the composition equation of Step 2. This is exactly the requested formal map: $b$ was the specified inverse projection followed by evaluation, $s$ its three successive transposes, and the last factor is the specified substitution of $c$. All of these arguments use just the lifted data on the domain in the question; none enlarges that domain or asserts a new invertibility theorem.

source.place: Sentence 4: the specific formal Verdier exchange is equivariant.

proof.text: Under the additional hypotheses of [fix-lem-tensor-adjunction, fix-cor-verdier-exchange], use their canonical exchange in the normalization [def-sf-verdier-exchange-data]. That definition specifies its arrow $\epsilon_M$ by projection and evaluation, exceptional transposition, substitution of $c$, then tensor–Hom and ordinary transposition. Moving substitution of $c$ past the latter two transposes changes neither map: for any adjunction $L\dashv R$, the unit formula gives $(v h)^\sharp=R(v)h^\sharp$, since both sides are $R(v)R(h)\eta$. Apply this first to $M\otimes-\dashv H_M$ and then to $P\dashv Q$. Therefore $\epsilon_M=e_M$, including the specified projection map and composition mate. In this normalization the internal-adjunction comparison has the direction stated in [fix-lem-tensor-adjunction], so the arrow from $D_YFM$ is its inverse followed by $QH_M(c)$, as specified by the auxiliary exchange in [def-sf-verdier-exchange-data]. The canonical isomorphism of [fix-cor-verdier-exchange] is, through its statement dependency [def-sf-verdier-exchange-data], a stage conclusion, whose components are by that definition exactly the arrows $\epsilon_M$; so its isomorphism assertion applies to this same arrow $\epsilon_M=e_M$. This invocation retains its exceptional admissibility and finite-Tor hypotheses only for this invertibility assertion.

source.place: Sentence 4 and fix-cor-verdier-exchange.proof.md Steps 1–2: normalization and conditional invertibility.

proof.text:
If $e_M$ is invertible, its Weil equation $e_M\theta_A=\theta_{QD_XM}P_Y(e_M)$ gives
$$e_M^{-1}\theta_{QD_XM}=\theta_AP_Y(e_M^{-1})$$
by the same multiplication as in Step 2. Thus its inverse is also equivariant. Steps 2–6 did not use the extra hypotheses of Step 7, so they also establish the stated equivariance on every domain supplying the displayed formal data. They used only rational Weil maps and lifted units/counits, never reduction of a rational Frobenius automorphism on an invariant integral lattice.
